Get organisation boundaries from OpenPrescribing

Source: R/openprescribing.R
get_op_boundaries.Rd

Downloads the geographic boundaries (or centroids / locations) that OpenPrescribing holds for organisations, ready to join to get_op_spending results by org_id == code for mapping.

Usage

get_op_boundaries(
  resolution = "icb",
  org = NULL,
  centroids = FALSE,
  as = c("sf", "geojson")
)

Arguments

resolution

one of "region", "icb", "sicbl", "pcn", "practice".

org

optional character vector of organisation codes to keep.

centroids

logical; return centroids instead of polygons (only honoured for Sub-ICB Locations).

as

"sf" (default; needs the sf package) or "geojson" for the raw GeoJSON text.

Value

An sf object in EPSG:4326 (WGS 84) with columns name, code and a geometry column, or the GeoJSON string.

Details

Region, ICB and PCN boundaries are unions of the underlying Sub-ICB (or practice) boundaries, so they are consistent with the OpenPrescribing organisation hierarchy but may differ slightly from the ONS generalised boundaries. Practices are returned as points.

Examples

# \donttest{
icb <- get_op_boundaries("icb")
#> Error: OpenPrescribing refused the request (HTTP 403, a bot-protection challenge), so no data could be retrieved from /org_location/.
#> This is applied by the service to some networks and clients (for example some cloud or institutional IP ranges). Try again later or from another network, and consider reducing the request rate with options(ukhsadatR.requests_per_second = 0.5).
plot(sf::st_geometry(icb))
#> Error: object 'icb' not found
# }
